## Example 2.4 {#dc2-example-2-4 .dc-lesson .dc-proof}

<p>Let <span data-math="y=\ln(f(x))"></span>.</p>
<div class="dc-proof-layout"><div class="dc-proof-prompts">
<p><strong>a)</strong> Let <span data-math="u=f(x)"></span>. Write <span data-math="y"></span> in terms of <span data-math="u"></span> and find <span data-math="\frac{dy}{du}"></span> and <span data-math="\frac{du}{dx}"></span>:</p>
<p><strong>b)</strong> Use the chain rule <span data-math="\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{dy}{du}\times\frac{du}{dx}"></span> to deduce a general rule for <span data-math="\frac{d}{dx}(\ln f(x))"></span>:</p>
</div><div class="dc-proof-working fragment" data-fragment-index="0">
<p><span data-math="y=\ln u,\qquad\frac{dy}{du}=\frac1u"></span></p>
<p><span data-math="\frac{du}{dx}={\color{#b55224}f^{\prime}(x)}"></span></p>
<p class="dc-final-rule"><span data-math="\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac1{f(x)}\cdot{\color{#b55224}f^{\prime}(x)}=\frac{{\color{#b55224}f^{\prime}(x)}}{f(x)}"></span></p>
<p class="dc-domain">For intervals where <span data-math="f(x)>0"></span>.</p>
</div></div><p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 11 · Example 2.4</p>

::: notes
Outer derivative is 1/u; inner derivative is f'(x). Substitute u=f(x) after multiplying: f'(x)/f(x). Keep the entire argument in the denominator. Reveal the complete proof as one chunk on Next. The orange numerator is the derivative of the whole argument. The function is ln f(x), defined where f(x)>0, and f must be differentiable there. Do not change the question to ln|f(x)|; the booklet explicitly distinguishes the later integral result involving an absolute value. About three minutes.
:::
